findings.title: The new downsize definition replaces the width/height API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods by argument signature: this second definition of `self.downsize` replaces the definition immediately above it. Existing calls using `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` now raise ArgumentError. Calls with just width and height instead treat the height as `opts`, which fails when `optimize` accesses `opts[:allow_animation]`. Preserve both calling conventions in a single method or give the dimensions-based entry point a different name.

findings.title: Downsizing can permanently remove animation from uploaded GIFs
findings.body: The upload's original file is overwritten using `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`. When animated thumbnails are disabled, the conversion reads only `from[0]`, so an oversized animated GIF becomes a single-frame image before it is stored. A setting governing thumbnails should not silently discard animation from the original upload. Preserve animation during upload downsizing, or reject an image that cannot be downsized without losing it.

findings.title: Percentage dimensions are not supported by the animated resizing command
findings.body: For a temporary file ending in `.gif` with `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled, this call selects gifsicle and passes `--resize-fit 80%`. Gifsicle's resize-fit option requires pixel dimensions in WIDTHxHEIGHT form, not a percentage. Conversion therefore fails, and the loop repeats the same failing operation five times without checking its result. Oversized animated GIFs remain oversized and cannot benefit from automatic downsizing. Calculate pixel dimensions for this path or use a command that supports percentage scaling.

findings.title: Keep attachment validation tied to the configured attachment limit
findings.body: The hard-coded 10 MB limit applies to attachments as well as images, although only images can be downsized. Sites configured to accept attachments larger than 10 MB now have those valid uploads blocked in the browser. Conversely, attachments exceeding a smaller configured limit are uploaded unnecessarily before being rejected by the server. Apply the expanded pre-downsizing allowance only to images and continue using `max_attachment_size_kb` for attachments.
